reviewer: desktop subagent independent read-only source review
scope: Only the original C18 private two-process PetPulse/PetDetails versus same-day Snapshot diagnostic plan and helper. This is separate from the product build and Browser IPC qualification.
method: Read complete authored PLAN.md, Rust helper, Python controller, binding template and manifest; inspect relevant production Pet Details semantics for the selected projection. Hash only these small authored inputs. No syntax check, compilation, SQL, database clone/read/hash, process probe, browser or application execution.

findings.evidence: run() starts rustc through Popen without a Job. On timeout or exception it kills and waits only for that Popen root. A Windows rustc link step may own link.exe descendants; the current root handle does not terminate or prove exit of those descendants.
findings.impact: The original compile timeout path can leave owned compilation work alive while returning a failed root result. It cannot establish that the CPU window is released or that all owned compiler descendants are reclaimed. No product source or acceptance threshold is implicated.
findings.requiredBoundary: Correct only a new private plan/controller copy: own the compiler process tree with a preconfigured kill-on-close Job, create suspended, assign before resume and clean up via owned handles on failure. Do not use global enumeration/kill. Preserve this original frozen plan, failure finding and hashes. The Core-only A/B helper does not itself start external subprocesses; its30s root timeout is a separate narrower case.
findings.rootDisposition: Root accepted the finding and assigned ledger a new private reviewfix copy; that unreviewed future copy is not qualified by this receipt.

verifiedStaticBoundaries.conclusion: Original DB and existing WAL are opened only GENERIC_READ with FILE_SHARE_READ, reject reparse, retain the same handles, and are never passed to Core::open. Rust Core receives fixed owned clones only.
FILETIME, file ID, volume and byte lengths use Python integer arithmetic; large identity fields are emitted as decimal strings, without JS Number rounding.

Once the original guard exists, its finally rereads the same handle/hash/size/identity, rechecks WAL0, source directory metadata and binding hash; a changed value raises and prevents completion. Failure during acquisition may lack a complete guard record and must remain a failed execution, not source-unchanged proof.

Exactly A and B directories/files use create-new semantics; both receive the same original read stream and are rehashed before Core::open. Marker/day/size/path and source overlap checks fence Rust access. Source body is not scanned.

Fixed expected current Shanghai day is checked before/after phases. A then B executes once each, with create-new result/failure files and no automatic retry. Selected values and primary binding digest compare exactly, while process-specific runtime/scope headers remain independently recorded.

A calls baseline Pulse, cursor Pulse and Details once each; B calls exactly one same-day Snapshot. Projection preserves false/null/zero distinctions through type-strict final JSON comparison, whole current-day unread truthiness, grouped issue count and stable latest-turn/nullable-TTFT selection. An empty current-day sample is retained rather than replaced by an easier historic date.
Snapshot serialization is streamed into a counting SHA writer, with only selected small fields retained. There is no second full serialized Snapshot byte buffer or full Snapshot file output.

Windows PrivateUsage is private committed bytes, distinct from working set. CPU uses raw GetProcessTimes100ns deltas and includes the sampler thread. Open/migration/backup, read phases, serialization and checkpoint are separately reported. Nominal2ms sampled peaks and max gap are descriptive, not formal gates.

Performance/full-import/M4 flags remain false. The source is the C15 incomplete partial-import405MB database; the plan does not inherit full-import, Native or historical C16 performance qualification.

pendingExecutionRequirements: bindings.frozen.json must be provided only after the actual C18 product/CLI and production rlib are frozen. This review has no actual C18 rlib/fingerprint/binary hash and does not qualify a future binding by filename.

Before execution, independently cross-check the actual productionLibraryReceipt, candidate receipt, precise custom-protocol production fingerprint, direct library hashes and native/transitive link paths. Current controller validates declared hashes but a hash alone does not prove semantic same-source linkage.
Root must release the CPU window. The current original bindings template is intentionally incomplete; missing or invalid frozen bindings fail closed.
The compiler descendant-cleanup correction requires its own new plan manifest/review. Do not overwrite or retroactively revise this original finding.
limitations: A readonly source review cannot prove Windows FFI ABI/runtime behavior, compilation, schema migration, comparison success or cleanup execution; no helper was run.

ReadGuard transfers ownership to a CRT fd before os.fdopen; an exceptional fdopen failure is not explicitly wrapped by a close guard. A failed invocation must never be promoted to successful post-verification; this is an additional defensive cleanup caveat, not the primary compiler-tree finding.

The wholeHelperSampledPeakPrivateBytes counter reflects asynchronous samples, while per-phase peaks also include endpoint observations; short peaks and phase-boundary attribution remain descriptive and should not be combined as an exact allocator maximum.
A30s helper timeout and180s compiler timeout do not constitute application performance thresholds. The parent may spend additional bounded cleanup time after timeout.
No original405MB database or raw logs were opened, cloned, hashed or changed during this review; only authored text and existing small metadata were read.
